newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end firm as market rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end firm as market rebounds.

text.p: Greek stocks closed 1.10 percent higher on Friday on moderate volume with the market pausing its correction to climb again close to 1,100 points. Brokers said momentum was strong and the rise could continue next week.

"The market opened with increased investment interest which was sustained throughout the session. The index rise was expected after Thursday's correction but late session buying was a positive sign," said George Pervanas, managing director at Pervanas Securities.
Another broker said that the end of the seamen's strike on Friday, also helped market sentiment with industrials pulling the index higher.

"We saw corrections in the last two sessions and a rebound was expected on Friday. Volume was quite satisfactory at 10.9 billion drachmas," said Antonis Sarris, managing director at A. Sarris Securities.
The Athens general share index closed 1.10 percent or 11.88 points up at 1092.31 from Thursday's 1080.43, after opening at 1080.70.

Most sectoral indices ended higher with banks gaining 0.32 percent, construction rising 0.61 percent and investment shares ending 1.52 percent up. Small caps ended 0.25 percent down but industrials gained 2.17 percent.
Friday's turnover was 10.9 billion drachmas on volume of 2.9 million shares. Losers led gainers 113 to 94 with 33 issues unchanged on 240 traded.
Cement companies performed strongly with Titan and Heracles rising 3.7 and 6.8 percent.
Sarris expects aluminium shares to perform well, because of the rise in international aluminium prices.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 836.00-854.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, rose 60 drachmas to close at 5,120.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $15.04-$16.04. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 6,706-7,111 drachmas.
